checks: The threshold box is compact and its finite cover constraint is closed. Each nonsaturated index has a witness satisfying exclusive equality, by the finite positive-gap argument. Such witnesses are distinct, since the same point cannot have two different exclusive equalities.

The strict complement is convex and its surviving trace is closed on P. Saturated caps have empty trace. The nonsaturated caps cover P outside T, and each has mass strictly less than τ since it is contained in its original cap.

A pair of same-label witnesses, or a witness paired with an equally labeled survivor, has its midpoint in P. The midpoint is outside the face because at least one endpoint is outside, and it strictly satisfies every complement inequality. This gives r+k(T)≤k without assuming disjointness of all inside and outside labels.

At τ=M/k the strict mass inequality rules out empty T and forces V(T)>k(T)M/k. For complete affine-lattice minors the inherited direction lattice is the intersection with the minor direction space, so any retained difference has the same parity relation as before.

With quotas on each proper face, the deepest-threshold set cannot lie in a proper face. If its convex hull missed the relative interior, an exposed support at a relative-interior point of the smaller hull would put that whole hull in a proper face. At rank zero the only point has depth M.

overlap.comparison: The accepted positive-set parity lemma gives the lattice face conclusion at τ=M/k by taking the exposing affine slack. Its proof has the same surviving-trace mechanism in that case. This frozen statement records the arbitrary-threshold certificate and permits general midpoint-closed labels.
The same general label condition yields an M/k center and an excess mass conclusion for some minimal face, without the outside-any-prescribed-face alternative, surviving trace or arbitrary threshold.
